A brake caliper (100) comprises first and second sections (104a, 104b) that accommodate two braking members (102a, 102b) between them. Its service-braking system uses at least two piston-cylinder units (108a, 110a; 108b, 110b), arranged as opposing pistons, to move the respective braking members (102a, 102b) toward a brake disc and thereby generate a service-braking force.

The caliper (100) further incorporates a parking-brake system. outputs.L3:
The brake caliper comprises first and second caliper parts configured to receive a pair of opposed braking members on opposite sides of a brake disc. A service brake mechanism includes at least two piston-and-cylinder assemblies arranged to force both braking members toward the brake disc during service braking.

The caliper further includes a park brake mechanism having an actuator configured to drive the first braking member toward the brake disc. A force-transmitting member transfers the driving force generated by the actuator to the second opposed braking member, thereby enabling both braking members to engage the disc during park braking. The force-transmitting member is slidably supported by an outer surface of a first cylinder and by a connecting member that extends between the first and second caliper parts.
outputs.L4:
A brake caliper includes first and second caliper parts arranged on opposite sides of a brake disc. Each caliper part supports a braking member and includes a cylinder containing a hydraulically actuated piston. During service braking, hydraulic pressure moves the opposed pistons toward the disc so that the braking members engage respective sides of the disc.

The caliper also incorporates a parking-brake actuator associated with one of the caliper parts. When operated, the actuator applies force to the braking member on that side of the disc. A force-transmitting component is mounted for sliding movement and transfers a corresponding reaction force to the opposing caliper part, thereby causing the other braking member to engage the opposite side of the disc. The force-transmitting component is supported and guided both by an outer surface of one of the cylinders and by a connecting member extending between the caliper parts. This dual support maintains the component in alignment, distributes the applied load, and permits reliable sliding movement. As a result, operation of the parking-brake actuator produces coordinated clamping of the disc by both braking members while preserving the opposed-piston arrangement used for service braking.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. Saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” refers to one that is already known or clearly identified.

Beyond grammar, “the” creates focus and significance. Expressions such as “the answer,” “the future,” or “the truth” suggest something unique and important. Although it often goes unnoticed, this simple word helps make language precise, connected, and meaningful.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style abstract describing a brake caliper with opposed-piston service braking and a separate park brake mechanism, retaining all reference numerals.
counterfactuals.output: A brake caliper (10) comprises a housing (12) straddling a brake rotor (14), first and second friction pads (16, 18), and opposed service pistons (20, 22) hydraulically movable to clamp the friction pads (16, 18) against the rotor (14). A park brake mechanism (24), separate from the hydraulic service-brake circuit (26), includes an actuator (28) and a force-transmission member (30) operable to mechanically displace at least one friction pad (16, 18) toward the rotor (14). The arrangement permits independent service and parking braking while providing a compact caliper assembly (10).

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical patent paragraph for a brake caliper in which a parking-brake actuator drives one brake pad and transmits force to the opposite pad through a member slidably supported by a cylinder and a caliper-spanning connector.
counterfactuals.output: A brake caliper assembly comprises a caliper body defining a cylinder and supporting first and second brake pads on opposite sides of a brake rotor, a parking-brake actuator operatively coupled to the first brake pad, a force-transmitting member slidably supported within the cylinder, and a caliper-spanning connector extending across the brake rotor and coupling the force-transmitting member to the second brake pad. Upon actuation of the parking-brake actuator, the first brake pad is urged toward a first side of the brake rotor, and a corresponding reaction force is transmitted through the force-transmitting member and the caliper-spanning connector to urge the second brake pad toward an opposite side of the brake rotor, thereby clamping the brake rotor between the first and second brake pads.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal engineering language, a combined service and parking brake caliper featuring two caliper parts, opposed pistons, and a sliding force-transfer arrangement.
counterfactuals.output:
A combined service and parking brake caliper comprises first and second caliper parts disposed on opposite sides of a brake rotor and coupled by a guide arrangement permitting relative sliding movement in an axial direction. Each caliper part supports at least one piston arranged in opposition to a piston of the other caliper part, the opposed pistons being operable to apply respective friction pads against opposite rotor faces during service braking.

A parking-brake actuator is integrated with one caliper part and is configured to generate an axial clamping force independently of, or in conjunction with, the service-brake pressure. A force-transfer member extends between the caliper parts and is mounted for sliding movement relative to at least one of them. Upon actuation of the parking-brake actuator, the force-transfer member transmits the actuator-generated force to the opposite caliper part, causing the opposed pistons or associated pads to clamp the rotor. The sliding connection accommodates pad wear, manufacturing tolerances, and relative caliper displacement while maintaining substantially balanced braking forces on the two rotor faces.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent claim covering a disc brake caliper with service-brake piston assemblies and a park-brake force transmitting member connected slidably to both a cylinder exterior and a connecting member.
counterfactuals.output: A disc brake caliper includes a caliper body supporting one or more service-brake piston assemblies, each having a cylinder and a piston movable within the cylinder to apply a braking force to a brake pad. A park-brake mechanism includes a force-transmitting member configured to transmit an actuating force for park-brake operation. The force-transmitting member is slidably connected to an exterior portion of at least one cylinder and is also slidably connected to a connecting member coupling the service-brake piston assemblies. The sliding connections guide movement of the force-transmitting member relative to the cylinder and the connecting member, enabling the park-brake force to be distributed through the caliper while permitting relative movement among the piston assemblies and associated components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
